author: Hotochin
text:
ok, so I think this is just an exercise of FTR to FTR and seeing which
 level gives first. There are a few things I don't see though like QM or
 CP. Here are my thoughts so far though. Follow price on the colored
lines from left to right please. I will do some more catching up later
when I get home.

1. Price comes down on the far left in yellow and makes a pole.

2. Price moves up in red

3. Price moves down in blue and almost touches the FL at 1.

4. Price moves up in purple and engulfs the FL marked 2. For the most
part the FL marked 1 held, and the FL marked 2 got engulfed, this is our
 sign of where price wants to go, up. Ultimately, I am thinking price
will return to the source of that engulf marked 5 to pick up more long
orders.

5. Price moves down in yellow and creates a FTR marked 4. Price also
engulfs the previous swing low. This is our clue that price wants to go
lower before higher.

6. Price then moves up in red and down in blue. This move is mid range
and ultimately is there to trick traders and pick up buy orders at the
FTR marked 6. Given this FTR is now tested, price should go to the FTR
at 5.

7. Before moving up. price has to take out supply at FTR marked 4. So price moves up in green to take that level out.

8. With the FTR at 6 out of the way, price can move all the way down in
yellow to pick up more orders at the source of the initial engulf of 2
at the FTR marked 5. Then price can blast up in purple to new highs.

God I hope this is right!

H

author: madwt
text:
Hi IF,

FO or Engulf?

Some people have interpreted the break of "A" as an engulf, yet others have interpreted it as a fake out.

In this
 post
you were asked what is the difference between an engulf and a fake out.
No answer was provided. I understand that an engulf involves price
making a lower low on reaction to Supply, or higher high on reaction to
Demand. More importantly, it shows intent of price to continue in the direction of the engulf.
 I also understand that a fake out occurs in order to find sufficient
liquidity to sell/buy against. More importantly, it is followed by a change in direction.

Knowing if the break of "A" is an engulf or fake out requires analysis
of the complete picture (higher time frames and looking left). However,
as neither of these are provided in the quiz, its mere speculation.

Taking the following chart as an example, would this be interpreted as
an engulf or as a fake out of "A" (or is it possible to be both)?

What is the difference between an engulf and fake out.

Thanks,

d
